Medicine-06.question: ১) Fever with night sweats is usually suggestive of which of the following?
Medicine-06.exp:
he correct answer is tuberculosis. Fever with night sweats is a classic constitutional symptom of tuberculosis, especially in chronic infections such as pulmonary TB.

Common features of TB:

  • Low-grade fever

  • Night sweats

  • Weight loss

  • Loss of appetite

  • Chronic cough (pulmonary TB)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Meningitis – Usually presents with headache, neck stiffness, altered consciousness, and acute fever.

  • Pneumonia – Typically causes acute fever, cough, sputum production, and respiratory symptoms.

  • Rheumatic fever – Presents with migratory polyarthritis, carditis, and other Jones criteria features.

High-yield points:

TB constitutional symptoms:

  • Fever (often evening rise)

  • Night sweats

  • Weight loss

  • Anorexia

Exam pearl:
Night sweats + chronic fever = Think tuberculosis.

Medicine-06.question: ২) Rapid diagnostic test is done for the diagnosis of which of the following?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is malaria. Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are widely used for the rapid diagnosis of malaria by detecting Plasmodium antigens in blood.

Common malaria RDT targets:

  • HRP-2 antigen → Plasmodium falciparum

  • pLDH antigen → Plasmodium species

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Kala-azar → Diagnosed by rK39 immunochromatographic test (also a rapid test), but in general exam context "rapid diagnostic test" most commonly refers to malaria RDT.

  • Typhoid → Diagnosed by blood culture; Widal test has limited value.

  • Tuberculosis → Diagnosed by sputum microscopy, GeneXpert MTB/RIF, culture.

High-yield points:

Disease Important rapid test
Malaria Malaria RDT (HRP-2/pLDH)
Kala-azar rK39 test
TB GeneXpert
Typhoid Blood culture

Exam pearl:
Rapid diagnostic test (RDT) in routine infectious disease MCQs = Malaria.

Medicine-06.question: ৩) Whih of the following is usually causes Peripheral Chest pain?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is pneumonia. Peripheral chest pain is typically pleuritic pain arising from irritation of the parietal pleura, which is supplied by somatic nerves and can localize pain to the chest wall.

Pneumonia involving the pleura commonly causes:

  • Sharp, localized chest pain

  • Pain worsened by deep inspiration or coughing

  • Peripheral chest pain

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Myocardial ischaemia (angina) → Causes central/retrosternal pressure-like pain due to visceral cardiac afferents.

  • Myocardial infarction → Causes severe central crushing chest pain, often radiating to arm/jaw.

  • Myocarditis → Usually causes diffuse chest discomfort or pain, not classically peripheral pleuritic pain.

High-yield points:

Types of chest pain:

  • Peripheral/pleuritic pain → Pleural inflammation (e.g., pneumonia, pleurisy)

  • Central crushing pain → Myocardial ischaemia/infarction

  • Sharp tearing pain → Aortic dissection

Exam pearl:
Peripheral chest pain = pleural irritation → Pneumonia.

Medicine-06.question: ৪) Tall stature is related to which of the following?
৫) On general examination, Thenar wasting is associated with which of the following?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is median nerve lesion. Thenar muscles are mainly supplied by the recurrent branch of the median nerve. Damage to the median nerve causes thenar wasting and loss of thumb opposition.

Features of median nerve lesion:

  • Thenar eminence wasting (ape thumb deformity)

  • Loss of thumb opposition

  • Sensory loss over lateral 3½ fingers

  • Commonly seen in carpal tunnel syndrome

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Ulnar nerve lesion → Causes hypothenar wasting and interosseous muscle wasting, leading to claw hand.

  • C8 lesion → May affect finger flexors and intrinsic hand muscles but is not the classic cause of thenar wasting.

  • T1 lesion → Mainly affects intrinsic hand muscles (especially interossei), not specifically thenar muscles.

High-yield points:

Finding Lesion
Thenar wasting Median nerve
Hypothenar wasting Ulnar nerve
Interosseous wasting Ulnar nerve (T1)
Ape thumb Median nerve

Exam pearl:
Thenar eminence wasting = Median nerve lesion.

Medicine-06.question: ৬) Which of the following Cardiac disease is associated with finger clubbing?
৭) Which of the following condition causes central cyanosis?
৮) Example of Intermittent fever is
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis). It is classically associated with intermittent fever, where fever spikes occur with periods of normal temperature in between.

Features of kala-azar:

  • Prolonged intermittent fever

  • Splenomegaly

  • Hepatomegaly

  • Pancytopenia

  • Weight loss

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Bronchopneumonia → Usually causes continuous or remittent fever.

  • Rheumatic fever → Fever may be present but not a classic intermittent fever pattern.

  • Typhoid fever → Classically causes step-ladder fever (progressive rise), followed by a sustained fever pattern.

High-yield fever patterns:

Fever pattern Example
Intermittent Kala-azar, malaria
Remittent Bronchopneumonia, infective diseases
Continuous Typhoid (classically)
Relapsing Malaria, Borrelia infection

Exam pearl:
Intermittent fever = Kala-azar / Malaria.

Medicine-06.question: ৯) Fever with Relative Bradycardia
১০) Cause of Nonpitting Oedema
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is myxoedema. Non-pitting oedema occurs due to deposition of mucopolysaccharides (glycosaminoglycans) in the tissues, which trap fluid and produce a firm, doughy swelling.

Myxoedema occurs in:

  • Hypothyroidism

  • Accumulation of hyaluronic acid and other glycosaminoglycans in skin and subcutaneous tissues

The other options are incorrect because:

  • CCF (congestive cardiac failure) → Causes pitting oedema due to fluid retention and increased venous pressure.

  • Nephrotic syndrome → Causes pitting oedema due to hypoalbuminaemia.

  • Hypoproteinaemia → Causes pitting oedema due to reduced plasma oncotic pressure.

High-yield points:

Type of oedema Examples
Non-pitting Myxoedema, lymphoedema
Pitting CCF, nephrotic syndrome, hypoproteinaemia

Exam pearl:
Non-pitting oedema = Myxoedema (hypothyroidism)

Medicine-06.question: ১১) Acute chest pain with nausea and sweating is seggestive of which of the following?
১২) Unilateral headache with aura is suggestive of
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is migraine. A unilateral headache associated with aura is a classic feature of migraine with aura.

Features of migraine:

  • Unilateral, throbbing headache

  • Aura before headache (visual symptoms such as flashing lights, zig-zag lines)

  • Nausea and vomiting

  • Photophobia and phonophobia

  • May be aggravated by physical activity

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Tension headache → Usually bilateral, pressing/tight band-like pain; no aura.

  • Meningitis → Causes severe headache with fever, neck stiffness, and systemic features.

  • Cluster headache → Severe unilateral orbital/temporal pain with autonomic symptoms (lacrimation, nasal congestion); aura is not typical.

High-yield points:

Headache type Key feature
Migraine Unilateral + aura
Tension headache Bilateral band-like pain
Cluster headache Unilateral orbital pain + autonomic signs
Meningitis Headache + fever + neck stiffness

Exam pearl:
Unilateral headache with aura = Migraine.

Medicine-06.question: ১৩) What is the initial investigation for a patient with sudden severe chest pain?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is ECG. In a patient with sudden severe chest pain, the initial investigation is a 12-lead ECG to rapidly assess for acute myocardial infarction (especially STEMI) and other cardiac causes.

Key points:

  • Should be performed within 10 minutes of arrival in suspected acute coronary syndrome.

  • Helps identify:

    • ST elevation

    • ST depression

    • T-wave changes

    • Arrhythmias

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Echo → Useful for assessing cardiac function, wall motion abnormalities, and complications, but not the first investigation.

  • ETT (Exercise tolerance test) → Used for stable chest pain evaluation, not acute severe chest pain.

  • X-ray → Helps detect other causes (pneumothorax, pneumonia, mediastinal pathology) but is not the first test for suspected ACS.

High-yield points:

Acute chest pain approach:

  1. 12-lead ECG (first investigation)

  2. Cardiac troponin

  3. Chest X-ray/other imaging as indicated

Exam pearl:
Sudden severe chest pain → ECG first.

Medicine-06.question: ১৪) Which one is the most common cause of acute berathlessness of a male smoker?
১৫) Rapid reccovery from a syncope(< 1 min) is usually suggestive of
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is neurocardiogenic syncope (vasovagal syncope). Rapid recovery within less than 1 minute is typical of syncope caused by transient reduction in cerebral blood flow, especially vasovagal episodes.

Features of neurocardiogenic syncope:

  • Brief loss of consciousness

  • Rapid spontaneous recovery

  • Often preceded by:

    • Sweating

    • Nausea

    • Dizziness

    • Feeling warm

  • Triggered by prolonged standing, emotional stress, pain

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Cardiac syncope → Often sudden with little/no warning and may have delayed recovery; associated with arrhythmias and structural heart disease.

  • Seizures → Recovery is usually slower with a post-ictal confused state, tongue biting, or incontinence.

  • Peripheral cause → Not a typical classification for syncope.

High-yield points:

Feature Neurocardiogenic syncope
Duration Brief
Recovery Rapid (<1 min)
Prodrome Sweating, nausea, dizziness
Common trigger Standing, emotion, pain

Exam pearl:
Syncope + rapid recovery + prodrome = Vasovagal (neurocardiogenic) syncope.

Medicine-06.question: ১৬) Minimum score on GCS score is
১৭) Cardiac tamponade causes which type of shock?
১৮) ACE inhibitor causes
১৯) Fever, cough, night sweats for 6 weeks is suggestive of
২০) Weight loss with pigmentation and hypotension is suggestive of which of the followings?
২১) Fever with Coated tongue is the feature of
২২) How many chamber in the heart?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is 4 chambers. The human heart consists of:

  1. Right atrium

  2. Right ventricle

  3. Left atrium

  4. Left ventricle

The right side pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs, while the left side pumps oxygenated blood to the systemic circulation.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • 2 chambers → Seen in simpler organisms, not humans.

  • 3 chambers → Seen in many amphibians.

  • 5 chambers → Not present in normal human heart.

High-yield points:

Human heart = 4 chambers

  • 2 atria

  • 2 ventricles

Exam pearl:
Normal human heart has four chambers.

Medicine-06.question: ২৩) QRS complex of 12 lead ECG represents which of the following?
২৪) Physiological cause of third heart sound is
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is pregnancy. A physiological third heart sound (S3) can occur due to increased blood volume and increased ventricular filling during pregnancy.

S3 occurs during:

  • Early diastolic rapid ventricular filling

  • Increased ventricular volume

Physiological S3 is seen in:

  • Pregnancy

  • Young adults

  • Children

The other options are incorrect because they are pathological causes:

  • Heart failure → S3 indicates volume overload and systolic dysfunction (“ventricular gallop”).

  • Mitral regurgitation → Increased ventricular volume can produce a pathological S3.

  • Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) → Ventricular dysfunction may cause S3.

High-yield points:

S3 heart sound:

  • Timing: Early diastole (after S2)

  • Mechanism: Rapid ventricular filling

  • Physiological: Pregnancy, young age

  • Pathological: Heart failure, MR, dilated cardiomyopathy

Exam pearl:
Physiological S3 = Pregnancy (and young healthy individuals).

Medicine-06.question: ২৫) First line investigation of stroke is
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is CT scan (non-contrast CT brain). The first-line investigation in suspected acute stroke is a non-contrast CT head to differentiate:

  • Ischaemic stroke

  • Intracerebral haemorrhage

This distinction is essential before starting thrombolytic therapy.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • MRI → More sensitive for early ischaemic changes, but usually not the initial investigation due to limited availability and longer scanning time.

  • ECG → Done to identify cardiac causes (e.g., atrial fibrillation) but not the primary brain imaging test.

  • EEG → Used for seizure evaluation, not stroke diagnosis.

High-yield points:

Acute stroke workup:

  1. Non-contrast CT brain (first imaging)

  2. Blood glucose

  3. ECG

  4. CT angiography/perfusion when indicated

Exam pearl:
Suspected stroke → CT brain first to rule out haemorrhage.

Medicine-06.question: ২৬) CVS cause of haemoptysis is
২৭) Most common cause of UTI is
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is Escherichia coli (E. coli). It is the most common cause of urinary tract infection (UTI), responsible for the majority of community-acquired UTIs.

Key points:

  • Source: Normal intestinal flora

  • Route: Ascending infection from perineum → urethra → bladder

  • Common in females due to shorter urethra

The other options are incorrect because:

  • S. typhi → Causes enteric fever, not a common UTI pathogen.

  • S. aureus → May cause UTI, especially with bacteraemia or instrumentation, but is uncommon.

  • S. epidermidis → Usually a skin contaminant; associated with prosthetic devices, not typical UTI.

High-yield points:

Common UTI organisms:

  1. E. coli (most common)

  2. Klebsiella

  3. Proteus

  4. Enterococcus

  5. Staphylococcus saprophyticus (young women)

Exam pearl:
Most common UTI organism = E. coli.

Medicine-06.question: ২৮) Persistent daily projectile vomiting, is usually due to
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is gastric outlet obstruction. Persistent daily projectile vomiting is a classic feature of obstruction at the pylorus or duodenum, where gastric contents cannot pass into the small intestine.

Features of gastric outlet obstruction:

  • Persistent vomiting (often large volume)

  • Projectile vomiting

  • Vomiting of undigested food

  • Early satiety

  • Weight loss

  • Visible gastric peristalsis (sometimes)

Common causes:

  • Peptic ulcer disease causing pyloric stenosis

  • Gastric carcinoma

  • Pancreatic malignancy

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Peptic ulcer disease → Can cause gastric outlet obstruction, but uncomplicated PUD does not typically cause persistent projectile vomiting.

  • Non-ulcer dyspepsia → Causes upper abdominal discomfort, bloating, early satiety; vomiting is not a dominant feature.

  • Gastric erosion → Usually causes bleeding or dyspepsia, not projectile vomiting.

High-yield points:

Projectile vomiting in adults → Think gastric outlet obstruction.

Exam pearl:
Persistent daily projectile vomiting = Gastric outlet obstruction.

Medicine-06.question: ২৯) Which of the following is responsible for hepatocelluler jaundice?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is paracetamol. Hepatocellular jaundice occurs due to damage to hepatocytes, causing impaired bilirubin uptake, conjugation, and excretion.

Paracetamol overdose causes:

  • Severe hepatocellular injury

  • Centrilobular hepatic necrosis

  • Marked elevation of AST/ALT

  • Hepatocellular jaundice

The other options are incorrect because they mainly cause obstructive (cholestatic) jaundice:

  • Choledocholithiasis → Obstruction of common bile duct → obstructive jaundice.

  • Parasitic infection (e.g., liver flukes) → May cause biliary obstruction/cholestasis.

  • Traumatic biliary strictures → Mechanical obstruction → obstructive jaundice.

High-yield points:

Type of jaundice Example
Hepatocellular Paracetamol toxicity, viral hepatitis, alcoholic hepatitis
Obstructive/cholestatic CBD stone, biliary stricture, pancreatic tumour
Haemolytic Malaria, hereditary haemolysis

Exam pearl:
Hepatocellular jaundice = hepatocyte injury → Paracetamol toxicity.

Medicine-06.question: ৩০) Jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, Pruritus is suggestive of which type of jaundice?
৩১) Which of the following is responsible for transudative ascites?
৩২) Which of the following is a non specific sign of anaemia?
৩৩) Subtype of Macrocytic anaemia is
৩৪) which of the following is a feature of LVF?
৩৫) First step of management of acute heart failure is ‘Sit the patient up’, why this step is taken for?
৩৬) Which one is a feature of Acute severe asthma?
৩৭) Which one is the preferred drug for isolated systolic hypertension?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is calcium channel blockers (CCBs). Isolated systolic hypertension (ISH) is common in the elderly and is mainly due to reduced arterial compliance (increased arterial stiffness).

Preferred antihypertensive drugs in ISH:

  • Long-acting calcium channel blockers (e.g., amlodipine)

  • Thiazide-like diuretics

CCBs are effective because they:

  • Reduce peripheral vascular resistance

  • Improve arterial compliance

  • Lower systolic blood pressure effectively

The other options are incorrect because:

  • α-blockers → Not preferred due to risk of postural hypotension, especially in elderly patients.

  • ACE inhibitors → Useful in hypertension with diabetes, CKD, or heart failure, but not the preferred first choice for isolated systolic hypertension.

  • β-blockers → Less effective for ISH in elderly patients and generally not first-line unless specific indications exist.

High-yield points:

Isolated systolic hypertension:

  • ↑ Systolic BP with normal/low diastolic BP

  • Common in elderly

  • Due to arterial stiffness

Preferred drugs:

  1. Calcium channel blockers

  2. Thiazide/thiazide-like diuretics

Exam pearl:
Elderly patient with isolated systolic hypertension → Calcium channel blocker (e.g., amlodipine).

Medicine-06.question: ৩৮) ACS includes..
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is All above. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is a spectrum of conditions caused by acute myocardial ischaemia due to reduced coronary blood flow.

ACS includes:

  1. ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)

    • Complete coronary artery occlusion

    • ST elevation on ECG

    • Myocardial necrosis

  2. Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI)

    • Partial occlusion or severe stenosis

    • Raised cardiac troponin

    • No ST elevation

  3. Unstable angina

    • Acute myocardial ischaemia without myocardial necrosis

    • Troponin remains normal

Medicine-06.question: ৩৯) Secondary prevention drug therapy for a myocardial infraction
৪০) which of the followings ia a cardinal biochemical feature of diabetic ketoacidosis?
Medicine-06.option2: ketonuria (more than 2+ on standard urine sticks)
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is hyperketonaemia (≥6.0 mmol/L). A cardinal biochemical feature of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is significant ketone accumulation due to increased lipolysis and hepatic ketone production.

Diagnostic features of DKA:

  1. Hyperglycaemia (usually glucose >13.9 mmol/L, but may be lower in euglycaemic DKA)

  2. Ketonaemia (blood ketones ≥3 mmol/L; severe DKA often ≥6 mmol/L)

  3. Metabolic acidosis (pH <7.3 or bicarbonate <18 mmol/L)

The other options are less appropriate:

  • Ketonuria (>2+ on urine sticks) → Can occur, but blood ketone measurement is preferred and urine ketones may underestimate severity.

  • Hyperglycaemia ≥30 mmol/L → Very high glucose is not a defining feature; DKA can occur with lower glucose levels.

  • Venous pH <7.1 → Indicates severe DKA, but not a universal cardinal feature.

High-yield points:

DKA triad:

  • Ketonaemia

  • Hyperglycaemia

  • Metabolic acidosis

Exam pearl:
Most important biochemical marker of DKA severity = Blood ketone level (β-hydroxybutyrate).

Medicine-06.question: ৪১) which of the following is not a features of hypoglycaemia?
৪২) Which one is the first step of management of Acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage?
Medicine-06.option3: I/V access using at least one large-bore cannula
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is establishing IV access with a large-bore cannula. The first priority in acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage (UGIH) is resuscitation and stabilization, following the ABC approach.

Initial management includes:

  • Secure large-bore IV access (preferably two large-bore cannulas)

  • Assess haemodynamic status

  • Send blood for FBC, coagulation profile, crossmatch

  • Start IV fluids/blood products as required

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Blood transfusion → Given if there is significant blood loss or haemodynamic compromise after assessment.

  • 1 L IV fluid running → Fluid resuscitation may be needed, but IV access must be established first.

  • Urgent endoscopy → Important for diagnosis and haemostasis, but performed after initial stabilization.

High-yield points:

Acute UGI bleed management:

  1. ABC + large-bore IV access

  2. Resuscitation (fluids/blood if indicated)

  3. Risk assessment

  4. Urgent endoscopy (usually within 24 hours after stabilization)

Exam pearl:
First step in acute GI haemorrhage = Secure large-bore IV access.

Medicine-06.question: ৪৩) Which anti diabetic drug doesn’t cause hypoglycaemia?
৪৪) Which of the following factor precipitate hepatic encephalopathy?
৪৫) Which of the following is a first line anti-TB drug?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is INH (Isoniazid). It is one of the first-line anti-tuberculosis (anti-TB) drugs used in the standard treatment regimen.

First-line anti-TB drugs (RIPE):

  • R → Rifampicin

  • I → Isoniazid (INH)

  • P → Pyrazinamide

  • E → Ethambutol

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Propofol → Intravenous anaesthetic agent.

  • Rifaximin → Non-absorbable antibiotic used mainly for hepatic encephalopathy and some diarrhoeal illnesses.

  • Ethosuximide → Antiepileptic drug used for absence seizures.

High-yield points:

First-line TB regimen = RIPE

  • Rifampicin

  • Isoniazid

  • Pyrazinamide

  • Ethambutol

Exam pearl:
INH = First-line anti-TB drug.

Medicine-06.question: ৪৬) SKin prick test is associated with wihich type of hypersensitivity reaction?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is Type-I hypersensitivity. A skin prick test is used to detect immediate (IgE-mediated) hypersensitivity reactions.

Mechanism:

  • Allergen introduced into skin

  • Allergen binds to IgE antibodies on mast cells

  • Mast cell degranulation occurs

  • Release of histamine and other mediators

  • → Wheal and flare reaction within minutes

Examples of Type-I hypersensitivity:

  • Allergic rhinitis

  • Bronchial asthma (atopic)

  • Anaphylaxis

  • Food allergy

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Type-II → Antibody-mediated cytotoxic reaction (e.g., autoimmune haemolytic anaemia, Goodpasture syndrome).

  • Type-III → Immune complex-mediated reaction (e.g., serum sickness, SLE).

  • Type-IV → Delayed T-cell mediated reaction (e.g., tuberculin skin test, contact dermatitis).

High-yield points:

Type Mechanism Example
Type I IgE + mast cells Skin prick test, allergy
Type II IgG/IgM against cells Autoimmune haemolysis
Type III Immune complexes SLE
Type IV T-cell mediated Mantoux test

Exam pearl:
Skin prick test = Type-I (IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity).

Medicine-06.question: ৪৭) Which of the following is the Preferred investigation for peptic ulcer disease?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is Upper GI endoscopy (OGD). It is the preferred investigation for peptic ulcer disease (PUD), especially in patients with alarm features, because it allows:

  • Direct visualization of gastric and duodenal ulcers

  • Biopsy to exclude malignancy (especially gastric ulcer)

  • Detection of complications (bleeding, obstruction)

  • Testing for H. pylori (e.g., rapid urease test from biopsy)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Rapid urease test → Detects H. pylori, but requires gastric biopsy and is not the primary investigation for diagnosing an ulcer.

  • Urea breath test → Non-invasive test for H. pylori eradication assessment or diagnosis, not for visualizing PUD.

  • Culture → Rarely used; mainly for antibiotic sensitivity testing of H. pylori.

High-yield points:

Investigation of PUD:

  • Upper GI endoscopy = diagnostic test of choice

  • Rapid urease test = detects H. pylori during endoscopy

  • Urea breath test = non-invasive H. pylori test

Exam pearl:
Peptic ulcer disease → Upper GI endoscopy is the preferred investigation.

Medicine-06.question: ৪৮) In a patient with aortic stenosis, which type of apex beat typically found?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is heaving apex beat. In aortic stenosis (AS), the left ventricle faces increased pressure overload, leading to concentric left ventricular hypertrophy.

A heaving (sustained) apex beat occurs due to:

  • Increased LV muscle mass

  • Forceful but prolonged ventricular contraction

  • Sustained pressure generation against the narrowed aortic valve

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Thrusting apex beat → Describes a hyperdynamic, forceful apex beat often seen in volume overload states (e.g., mitral regurgitation, aortic regurgitation).

  • Dyskinetic apex beat → Suggests ventricular aneurysm or severe LV dysfunction with abnormal outward movement.

  • Normal → Not expected in significant aortic stenosis.

High-yield points:

Condition Apex beat
Aortic stenosis Heaving, sustained
Aortic regurgitation Hyperdynamic/thrusting
Dilated cardiomyopathy Displaced, diffuse
LV aneurysm Dyskinetic

Exam pearl:
Pressure overload (AS) → concentric LVH → heaving apex beat.

Medicine-06.question: ৪৯) What is the earliest change of ECG folloing Myoardial infraction?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is ST segment elevation. The earliest ECG change following acute myocardial infarction (MI) is usually hyperacute T waves, followed by ST segment elevation (in transmural MI/STEMI).

Typical ECG sequence after MI:

  1. Hyperacute T waves (earliest, minutes)

  2. ST segment elevation (minutes to hours)

  3. T wave inversion (hours to days)

  4. Pathological Q waves (hours to days; indicate myocardial necrosis)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • T inversion → A later change after the acute phase.

  • Q wave change → Develops later and indicates established infarction/necrosis.

  • ST-segment deviation → General term; in acute STEMI, the specific early change is ST elevation.

High-yield points:

MI ECG progression:
Hyperacute T wave → ST elevation → T inversion → Q wave

Exam pearl:
Earliest classic ECG finding in acute STEMI = ST segment elevation.

Medicine-06.question: ৫০) which factor other than disease can influence investigation results?
Medicine-06.exp:
The correct answer is All above. Investigation results can be influenced by several patient-related factors other than disease, including:

  • Body weight → Can affect drug levels, biochemical parameters, and reference ranges.

  • Malnutrition → May alter albumin, electrolytes, blood counts, and enzyme levels.

  • Sex → Physiological differences can influence normal laboratory values (e.g., haemoglobin, creatinine).

Other factors that may affect investigations:

  • Age

  • Pregnancy

  • Time of sample collection

  • Medications

  • Exercise

  • Hydration status

High-yield points:

Non-disease factors affecting investigation results:

  • Age

  • Sex

  • Body weight

  • Nutrition status

  • Drugs

  • Biological variation

Exam pearl:
Body weight + malnutrition + sex can all influence investigation results → All above.
